title: A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis.
abstract: It has long been known that poxviruses transcribe more than a hundred early mRNAs within their viral core, yet how these transcripts exit the core remains unknown. Here, we combine cryo-electron tomography with deep-learning-based particle picking, subtomogram averaging, cross-linking mass spectrometry, and AlphaFold3 modeling to resolve the molecular architecture of a long-sought pore within the poxvirus core. The pore is formed by a heteromeric assembly of the viral proteins E8, E6, and L3, which together create a hollow hexameric tube spanning both the core wall and the surface-exposed palisade layer. Within the pore channel, we observe a rod-like density consistent with the viral RNA helicase I8, which may contribute to the release of the newly synthesized viral mRNAs from the core. We further observe a state of the pore lacking the outer and basal rings under transcription conditions. Together, our findings identify the structure and dynamics of a candidate mRNA-release pore within the surface layer of a double-stranded DNA virus and suggest that it may form part of the poxvirus transcription machinery.

title: Cinobufagin induces peroxisome dysfunction through suppression of the peroxisomal biogenesis factor proteins and interferes with lipid metabolism to affect the growth of liver cancer cells.
abstract: Primary liver cancer is the sixth most commonly diagnosed cancer and the third most common cause of cancer death worldwide. Chansu is made by processing and drying the white serous fluid of the posterior ear and skin glands of Bufo bufo gargarizans Cantor or Bufo melanostictus Schneider. Chansu is a well-known traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) that is mainly used for detoxification, detumescence, analgesia, the treatment of cancer, and heart failure. Cinobufagin, as a bufadienolide, has been reported as the main antitumor active component of Chansu. However, the molecular mechanisms related to the anticancer effects of cinobufagin still remain elusive. The purpose of this study is to explore whether cinobufagin inhibits the growth of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells by inducing peroxisome dysfunction and interfering with lipid metabolism. The protein levels of catalase, ABCD3, PEX5, PEX6, and PEX10 in human hepatoma cells were analyzed by Western blotting. The effects of cinobufagin on the viability of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 cells were detected by cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assay and clone formation assay. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) transfection was used to explore whether inhibition of PEX could enhance the inhibitory effect of cinobufagin on cell growth of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells. The effects of cinobufagin on lipid metabolism were analyzed by untargeted metabolomics. The in vivo antitumor effects of cinobufagin were verified by animal studies. Cinobufagin causes peroxisome dysfunction in HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells. From a mechanistic point of view, we reveal that cinobufagin downregulates the expression of PEX5, PEX10, and PEX6. In addition, through RNA interference, cinobufagin partially blocks the growth of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells and restrains the expression of lipid metabolism-related proteins via downregulating the expression of PEX5 and PEX10. Subsequently, we perform a non-targeted metabolomics analysis of the cells and find that cinobufagin exerts its anti-hepatoma effects by interfering with lipid metabolic reprogramming. The results show that cinobufagin mainly interferes with glycerophospholipid and fatty acyl levels. In addition, in vivo experiments reveal that cinobufagin restrains tumor growth without obvious adverse effects. Serum metabolomics analyses reveal that cinobufagin causes significant changes in the levels of lipid and lipid-like differential metabolites. Cinobufagin is a promising natural drug for the treatment of liver cancer, and PEXs may be potential molecular targets of cinobufagin to exert anticancer effects. Cinobufagin induces peroxisome dysfunction through suppression of the proteins encoded by the PEX genes and interferes with lipid metabolism to restrain the growth of liver cancer cells.

title: Loss of splicing factor SR45 reshapes tissue-dependent alternative polyadenylation landscapes and transcriptome responses to salt in Arabidopsis.
abstract: Serine/arginine-rich 45 (SR45) is a plant-specific SR-like splicing factor and an RNA-binding protein involved in Arabidopsis development and stress responses. Although SR45 has been primarily studied for its role in pre-mRNA alternative splicing (AS), whether it also regulates alternative polyadenylation (APA) remains unclear. Here, we combined poly(A) tag sequencing (PAT-seq) and RNA-seq to examine APA, AS, and gene expression in wild-type (WT) and sr45-1 plants across inflorescence, leaf, and root under normal conditions, and in leaf and root under prolonged mild salinity. Under normal conditions, SR45 loss caused widespread changes in poly(A) site usage, with distal site shifts occurring more frequently than proximal shifts across tissues. APA, AS, and differential gene expression showed only partial overlap, with significant enrichment between APA and AS but not with gene expression changes, indicating that APA represents a distinct layer of SR45-mediated transcriptome regulation. Under prolonged mild salinity conditions, pairwise analyses showed preference of distal poly(A) site usage in WT and proximal site usage in sr45-1, particularly in leaf. Replicate-aware genotype-by-treatment interaction analyses further identified genotype-dependent differences in APA and gene expression, where more genotype-treatment interacting genes detected in leaf than in root. Genes encoding polyadenylation and splicing factors also showed changes in APA, AS, or transcript abundance. Together, these results expand the known role of SR45 from splicing regulation to APA-associated transcriptome remodeling and reveal that SR45 is required for proper salt-responsive changes in transcript abundance in Arabidopsis.

title: RNA recognition and cleavage in archaeal ribosome biogenesis: insights from FAU-1.
abstract: Ribosomal RNA maturation requires nucleases that recognize appropriate precursors and cleave them at defined stages of ribosome assembly. How these activities are organized in archaea remains elusive. Kawai and colleagues determined the crystal structure of the archaeal ribonuclease FAU-1, revealing a homotrimer with peripheral RNA-binding domains and a central assembly formed by its C-terminal domains. The structure identifies similarities to the RNA-recognition region of bacterial ribonuclease (RNase) E while exposing substantial differences in overall architecture. Subsequent work assigned FAU-1 to the RNase W family and demonstrated a catalytic role for its C-terminal domain. Together, these studies illustrate how related RNA-recognition elements can operate within distinct nuclease architectures. They also raise questions about the relationship between oligomerization, substrate selection and catalytic activation. Resolving these questions will require analysis of physiological RNA substrates and their associated proteins, connecting the structures of individual processing enzymes to the assembly of functional ribosomes.

title: Ribosome structure, function and dysfunction at the molecular level.
abstract: Ribosomes are essential ribonucleoprotein complexes that translate genetic information into proteins and are therefore central to cellular growth, development, and homeostasis. Recent advances in structural biology and genomics have transformed our understanding of ribosomes from static translational machines to highly dynamic complexes whose assembly, function, and quality control are tightly regulated. In this review, we provide an overview of eukaryotic ribosome structure and biogenesis, focusing on insights gained from yeast and human systems. We discuss the hierarchical assembly of ribosomal subunits, rRNA processing and modification, nuclear export, and cytoplasmic maturation. Particular emphasis is placed on the surveillance mechanisms that monitor ribosome assembly, including structural proofreading, molecular mimicry, RNA decay pathways, and translation-like "test-drive" reactions that assess ribosome competence. We further examine how defects in ribosome biogenesis and translation activate nucleolar surveillance, ribosome quality-control pathways, and downstream stress-response networks, including p53 signaling, the integrated stress response, and ribotoxic stress pathways. Together, these mechanisms form an interconnected quality-control system that safeguards ribosome function and cellular protein homeostasis. These studies provide important insights into the molecular basis of numerous ribosomal diseases and related disorders associated with defective ribosome biogenesis and function. Finally, we highlight emerging questions regarding ribosome heterogeneity, specialization, and the relationship between ribosome quality control and human disease.

title: Codon optimization as a design variable in biotherapeutics.
abstract: Codon optimization (CO) is a key design variable in biotherapeutics that is used to enhance expression of recombinant proteins, gene therapies, and vaccines. Although synonymous codon substitutions were historically considered neutral, codon choice can influence messenger RNA (mRNA) stability, translation kinetics, cotranslational folding, and immunogenicity. Current optimization strategies integrate computational parameters including codon adaptation indices, tRNA availability, mRNA structure, cytosine-phosphate-guanine dinucleotide content, codon pair bias, and machine learning approaches to balance expression and product quality. Additionally, dynamic tRNA modifications within the epitranscriptome modulate codon-biased translation in a context-dependent manner. While CO has not been implicated in adverse clinical outcomes, its context-dependent effects on protein conformation, post-translational modifications, and immune responses necessitate rigorous characterization. This opinion article presents our viewpoint on mechanisms, applications, and regulatory considerations for CO in biologics.

title: CellMethMarker provides an integrated database of human cell- and tissue-type-specific DNA methylation markers
abstract: Cell- and tissue-type-specific DNA methylation markers provide epigenetic signatures of cellular identity and are widely used to infer cellular origin from bulk and single-cell methylomes. Existing resources mainly emphasize disease-associated biomarkers, methylome atlases, genomic annotations or RNA-based cell markers, leaving an unmet need for an integrated region-level resource dedicated to such markers. Here we present CellMethMarker (http://gu-zhanglab.hfcas.ac.cn/CellMethMarker), a curated database integrating 347,514 de novo markers derived from uniformly processed whole-genome and reduced-representation bisulfite sequencing datasets, 2,203,507 literature-derived marker records and harmonized metadata for 2,810 samples. CellMethMarker enables cell- and tissue-centered marker retrieval, coordinate-based search, genome-browser visualization, interactive methylation analysis and data download. In an independent single-cell methylome atlas, these markers recover the expected cell-type-associated methylation patterns, and a platform-matched reference built from them lowers the mean deconvolution error from 0.365 to 0.144. CellMethMarker therefore links region-level DNA methylation variation to cellular identity and supports methylome-based cell-type annotation and deconvolution.

title: RBM47-Mediated Stabilization of PARP1 mRNA Exacerbates Subarachnoid Hemorrhage With RBM47 Transcriptionally Regulated by EGR1.
abstract: Early brain injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is chiefly marked by neuronal apoptosis and neuroinflammation, while the principal regulating molecules have yet to be identified. RBM47 exhibited considerable upregulation in the cerebral cortex of SAH mice and hemoglobin (Hb)-induced primary cortical neurons. Knockdown of RBM47 with intracerebroventricular injection of small interfering RNA improved neurobehavioral scores (modified Garcia score and beam balance test), mitigated brain edema and SAH grade, and decreased the quantity of FJC-positive and TUNEL-positive neurons in the cortex. Furthermore, RBM47 knockdown suppressed the expression of apoptotic proteins, obstructed HMGB1 nuclear to cytoplasmic translocation, and reduced TNF-α and IL-6 concentrations. In vitro results further validated that RBM47 knockdown diminished Hb-induced neuronal apoptosis and neuroinflammation. The transcription factor EGR1 directly bound to the RBM47 promoter and transcriptionally stimulated RBM47. RBM47 enhanced PARP1 expression by binding to the 3'UTR of PARP1 mRNA. Co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated a connection between PARP1 and HMGB1, facilitating HMGB1 release. We conducted label-free proteomics analysis on primary neurons following PARP1 knockdown and Hb therapy. Differentially expressed proteins were enriched in ADP ribosylation, regulation of necroptosis, and the extrinsic apoptotic pathway. GSEA revealed a large negative enrichment of the neuronal apoptotic process, while pathways associated with mitochondrial activity exhibited highly significant positive enrichment. EGR1 transcriptionally stimulates RBM47, which then enhances HMGB1 release by upregulating PARP1, therefore facilitating neuronal death and inflammation following SAH. PARP1 knockdown alters the mitochondrial protein expression profile and inhibits apoptosis and necroptosis. Targeting the EGR1/RBM47/PARP1/HMGB1 axis may provide an innovative therapeutic approach for SAH.

title: Molecular Characterization and Regulatory Role of UBE2A in Inflammatory Responses in the Manila Clam (Ruditapes philippinarum).
abstract: Ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 A (UBE2A) is a core component of the ubiquitination machinery that plays an important role in innate immunity, however, its immune function in the bivalve mollusk Ruditapes philippinarum has not been experimentally defined. In this study, we identified a UBE2A homolog (RpUBE2A) encoding a protein with a conserved ubiquitin-conjugating (UBC) domain. Phylogenetic analysis placed RpUBE2A within the molluscan UBE2A clade. RpUBE2A was constitutively expressed across all examined tissues, with highest transcript levels in immune-related tissues, particularly the gill and siphon. Following Vibrio parahaemolyticus challenge, both RpUBE2A mRNA and protein were significantly upregulated. Functional assays revealed that RpUBE2A overexpression enhanced global ubiquitination, upregulated the key inflammatory cytokine RpIL-17, and increased inflammatory cell infiltration as evidenced by H&E staining, whereas it significantly reduced cell viability. Conversely, RNA interference-mediated knockdown of RpUBE2A markedly attenuated the inflammatory response triggered by V. parahaemolyticus challenge. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that RpUBE2A is rapidly induced upon infection and, through modulating inflammatory genes and ubiquitination, serves as a positive regulator of the antibacterial innate immune response, likely contributing to the initiation and amplification of gill inflammation during V. parahaemolyticus challenge. These results reveal a previously unrecognized immune function for UBE2A and provide the first evidence for UBE2A-dependent host-pathogen interactions in bivalves.

title: Esketamine alleviates the pain-depression dyad: insights from exploratory transcriptomic profiling and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations within the anterior cingulate cortex.
abstract: The molecular mechanisms driving esketamine (ESK) efficacy in the pain-depression dyad (PDD) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of a sub-anesthetic ESK regimen on cortical expression profiles and exploratory signaling markers within the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized into Sham, PDD, and PDD + ESK groups. The PDD model, established via chronic constriction injury (CCI), was validated using a behavioral test battery tracking mechanical allodynia and depression-like phenotypes. On day 21 post-surgery, PDD + ESK rats received a single esketamine injection (15 mg/kg, i.p.). Multi-regional c-Fos expression mapping across the PFC, HPC, and ACC identified the primary responsive structure, followed by dual immunofluorescence for cellular phenotyping. Finally, ACC excitatory neuronal calcium dynamics, exploratory transcriptomic profiles, and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations (including GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation alongside synaptic markers) were evaluated using fiber photometry, RNA sequencing, and Western blotting. ESK alleviated pain hypersensitivity, behavioral despair, and anhedonia in PDD rats. Regional c-Fos profiling identified the ACC as the primary reactive locus, with activation localized predominantly to CaMKIIα-positive neurons. Fiber photometry confirmed that ESK attenuated functional hyperactivation in these ACC excitatory neurons. Exploratory transcriptomic profiling (unadjusted P < 0.05) revealed candidate altered transcripts, identifying Wnt4 as an exploratory molecular marker for further investigation. Subsequent orthogonal protein validations demonstrated that ESK modulated Wnt4 expression alongside concomitant alterations in GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation, parallel with the attenuation of pathologically elevated synaptic protein markers and a restorative trend in synaptic ultrastructure. A single sub-anesthetic ESK dose effectively alleviates PDD behavioral phenotypes in rats. This therapeutic efficacy is associated with Wnt4-related molecular adjustments coupled with putative downstream GSK3β-mTOR signaling alterations within the ACC CaMKIIα-positive neurons, providing exploratory transcriptomic and molecular insights into cortical adaptations in pain-related affective disorders.

title: Glia proliferation and heterogeneity in CMT1A: Involvement of RUNX2-Schwann cells and endoneurial fibroblasts.
abstract: Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 1 A (CMT1A) is the most common inherited peripheral neuropathy, caused by duplication of the peripheral myelin protein 22 (PMP22) gene and characterized by dysmyelination and defects in myelin maturation. Hypercellularity, defined as an abnormal increase in the number of cells within a tissue, is a prominent feature of the disease, although its origin, persistence, and underlying mechanisms remain controversial. Here, we performed a time-course analysis of sciatic nerves from wild-type (WT) and CMT1A rats between 2 and 12 months of age. We demonstrated that CMT1A nerves exhibit persistent cellular proliferation extending into adulthood. This phenotype is confirmed by bulk RNA-seq data showing sustained enrichment of proliferation-associated gene signatures. Cell-type signature analysis identifies overrepresentation of immature, neural crest-related, and epithelial-mesenchymal transitional (EMT) transcriptional programs in CMT1A nerves. Among the most upregulated genes, RUNX2 showed strong and prolonged expression at both transcript and protein levels. Consistently with the key role of RUNX2 in the activation of the injury response, CMT1A nerves also showed a marked enrichment both in SOX10+/JUN+ cells and in SOX10+/RUNX2+ cells, indicating a maladaptive activation of the injury-like Schwann cell (SC) program. Interestingly, we detected robust upregulation of SMOC2, an extracellular matrix protein selectively expressed by endoneurial fibroblasts, pointing to activation of non-canonical cell types and altered extracellular matrix remodeling. Together, these data demonstrate that CMT1A peripheral nerves are characterized by chronic hypercellularity associated with persistent proliferation, EMT, and dysregulated injury transcriptional programs, collectively pointing at progressive and multicellular nerve remodeling as a relevant pathomechanism in the disease.

title: Beyond the liver: Hepatitis E virus-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome with respiratory failure in an adolescent, a case report.
abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) remains endemic worldwide, especially in resource-constrained settings. Although HEV-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is well documented in adults, severe presentations in adolescents are scarcely reported. A previously healthy 12-year-old female presented with progressive ascending weakness and rapidly progressive respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation. Acute hepatitis E infection was diagnosed based on positive anti-HEV IgM antibodies, confirmed by detection of HEV RNA on real-time reverse-transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR). Cerebrospinal fluid protein and cell count were normal, consistent with early-stage GBS. A diagnosis of HEV-associated GBS was made. Despite intravenous immunoglobulin therapy and intensive supportive care, the clinical course remained severe, and the patient ultimately died after withdrawal of care due to financial constraints. HEV is an under-recognized trigger for severe GBS in adolescents, and should be considered in cases of acute flaccid paralysis presenting with concurrent hepatic dysfunction. Early recognition, therefore, remains paramount, particularly in resource-limited, endemic regions, where delayed diagnoses may result in poor clinical outcomes.

title: Pharmacological profiling reveals sensitivity of vitamin D/TGF-β cooperative gene regulation to epigenetic and transcription-associated inhibitors.
abstract: Synergistic gene regulation by the active vitamin D metabolite, 1,25(OH)2D3 and transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) has been reported for a limited number of target genes. Among these, 5-lipoxygenase (5-LO), a key enzyme in leukotriene biosynthesis and innate immune signaling, represents a well-established example of this cooperative regulation. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this synergy between vitamin D and TGF-β remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the involvement of chromatin-associated and transcriptional regulators in 1,25(OH)2D3/TGF-β mediated gene regulation in monocytic cell lines. Pharmacological perturbation revealed sensitivity of the cooperative response to inhibition of epigenetic regulators, including class I histone deacetylases (HDACs), bromodomain-containing proteins (BRDs), as well as molecular chaperone heat shock protein (HSP90) and transcriptional/signaling kinases such as cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 9 and mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs). Further analysis demonstrated differential regulation of ALOX5 (5-LO), CD14 (CD14) and CXCL8 (interleukin-8 (IL-8)) upon modulation of these regulatory pathways in the monocytic cell lines MonoMac-6 and THP-1. RNA-Sequencing identified additional genes synergistically regulated by combined 1,25(OH)2D3/TGF-β stimulation that were enriched for immune-related functions and displayed similar sensitivity to pharmacological disruption of transcriptional and chromatin regulatory mechanisms. Furthermore, VDR knockout experiments demonstrated that intact VDR signaling is required for 1,25(OH)2D3/TGF-β mediated cooperative gene regulation. These findings reveal a broader set of immune-associated genes regulated by 1,25(OH)2D3/TGF-β cooperation and identify chromatin and transcriptional regulators as important modulators of this response in monocytic cells.

title: Regulatory network remodeling and potential non-canonical associations of the transcription factor SP1 during inflammation-to-cancer transformation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is closely linked to chronic inflammation, but the transcriptional mechanisms connecting epithelial inflammatory remodeling with malignant transformation remain incompletely understood. We integrated secondary analysis of published single-cell epithelial transition-state data, virtual SP1 perturbation, TCGA analyses, xCell immune infiltration analysis, TIDE-based exploratory immunotherapy prediction, Co-IP/MS, and a 4NQO-induced mouse model to investigate SP1-associated network remodeling during ESCC carcinogenesis. SP1 regulatory importance increased across pairwise epithelial state comparisons. In adjacent normal epithelial cells, virtual SP1 overexpression affected genes linked to inflammatory response, NF-κB-related signaling, epithelial stress remodeling, and proliferation. SP1 expression correlated with immune infiltration features and immune checkpoint gene expression, and TIDE analysis suggested an association with predicted immunotherapy-related features. SP1-binding partners were enriched in RNA metabolism, RNA splicing, and nuclear protein-complex annotations, suggesting potential non-canonical regulatory associations that require further experimental validation. SP1 may represent a progressively enhanced transcriptional hub during inflammation-associated ESCC carcinogenesis, with state-dependent network remodeling spanning epithelial inflammatory stress, malignant transformation, and tumor immune features.

title: CMTM6 regulates hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis through modulating IFNRs-STAT1-KLF4 signaling axis.
abstract: CMTM6 is known to stabilize PD-L1 on cancer cells, facilitating immune evasion, but its role in normal hematopoiesis remains unexplored. Hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) homeostasis is tightly regulated by interferon (IFN) signaling, yet the mechanisms controlling IFN receptor stability are unclear. In this study we investigated whether CMTM6 regulates HSC maintenance and elucidated the underlying molecular pathways. Using a conditional Cmtm6 knockout mouse model (Vav-Cre), we performed flow cytometry, competitive transplantation, single-cell RNA sequencing, co-immunoprecipitation, and functional assays on bone marrow HSCs. Cmtm6 deficiency led to increased HSC proliferation but impaired reconstitution capacity, accompanied by elevated DNA damage and disrupted cell polarity. Single-cell analysis revealed a marked reduction in IFN response pathways. Mechanistically, CMTM6 directly interacted with IFNAR1 and IFNGR1, stabilizing their protein expression. Downstream, Cmtm6 deletion impaired STAT1 phosphorylation and reduced KLF4 expression; single-cell analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between Stat1 activity and Klf4 expression, and STAT1 inhibition in HSCs confirmed that STAT1 activity is required for maintaining KLF4 expression. Notably, KLF4 overexpression partially rescued colony-forming defects and reduced γH2AX foci in Cmtm6-deficient HSCs, identifying KLF4 as a key downstream effector. Additionally, we observed accompanying molecular changes including reduced SIAH2, elevated DYRK2, decreased c-MYC, and increased P53, which may contribute to the observed phenotypes. These findings demonstrate that CMTM6 maintains HSC homeostasis by stabilizing IFN receptors and regulating the IFNR-STAT1-KLF4 signaling axis, revealing a novel physiological function for CMTM6 in hematopoiesis.

title: Benzoylaconine suppresses colorectal cancer progression by modulating the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) has a high incidence, and both metastasis and drug resistance remain formidable challenges in clinical management. Owing to their multi-target activity and favorable safety profiles, natural products have become a prolific source for anticancer drug discovery. Benzoylaconine (BAC) is a secondary metabolite of aconitine with markedly attenuated toxicity that retains anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antitumor properties; however, its antitumor effects and the underlying molecular mechanisms in CRC are poorly defined. This study was designed to systematically characterize the impact of BAC on the malignant phenotypes of CRC cells and to identify its potential molecular targets. HCT116 and SW480 cells were used as model systems. Proliferation was assessed by MTT and EdU assays; migration and invasion by wound-healing and Transwell assays, respectively; cell cycle and apoptosis by flow cytometry. Network pharmacology was applied to predict core targets and construct a protein-protein interaction network. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations examined binding; SPR verified direct binding to CDK2 and MMP2. RNA-seq identified differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways. Western blotting validated key protein changes. Patient-derived CRC organoids (PDOs) were established to evaluate BAC efficacy; organoid viability was assessed by CellTiter-Glo® 2.0 assay, and morphology by bright-field microscopy. BAC dose- and time-dependently inhibited CRC cell proliferation and EdU positivity, slowed wound closure, and reduced Transwell invasion, indicating impaired migration and invasion. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that BAC induced G1/S cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Network pharmacology identified CDK2 and MMP2 as key targets; molecular dynamics and SPR confirmed stable binding (KD ≈ 3.9 and 4.4 μM). RNA-seq showed enrichment of pathways related to cell cycle regulation and tumor invasion. Western blotting revealed that BAC dose-dependently downregulated CDK2, CDK6, MMP2, Cyclin E1, and Cyclin D1, and upregulated p21. BAC also inhibited the proliferation of colorectal cancer organoids. BAC induces G1/S cell cycle arrest in CRC cells, likely through modulation of the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis, thereby suppressing proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis, and may represent a promising lead for CRC therapy.

title: Targeting the gut-tumor axis: probiotic therapy as an adjunct strategy in colorectal cancer treatment.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a multifactorial disease driven by interactions among host genetics, immune dysregulation, environmental factors, and gut microbiota. The gut-tumor axis regulates CRC progression through inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier disruption, and immune imbalance. Probiotic-derived metabolites act as bioactive molecules capable of restoring host-microbiome homeostasis and modulating tumor-associated pathways. To evaluate probiotic metabolites as adjunct therapeutic agents in CRC using integrative multi-omics analysis and in vitro validation. A systems biology approach integrating network pharmacology, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiome profiling was applied. Twelve probiotic metabolites yielded 428 predicted targets, with 162 overlapping CRC-associated genes. CRC cell lines (HCT116, HT-29, Caco-2, SW480) were treated and analyzed for viability, apoptosis, gene/protein expression, cytokines, metabolites, and microbial composition. Sodium butyrate (5 mM) reduced cell viability by 35.5-42.3% (p < 0.001) and increased apoptosis from 8.6% to 32.4%, reaching 41.2% when combined with indole-3-acetic acid (IAA, 100 μM), suggesting a synergistic pro-apoptotic effect. RNA-seq identified 1,248 DEGs, with upregulation of BAX and CASP3 (log2FC +1.8 to +2.3) and downregulation of IL6, TNF, and NFKB1 (-1.5 to -2.1). Proteomics revealed 412 differentially expressed proteins, including downregulation of AKT1 (-1.6-fold), MAPK1 (-1.4-fold), and EGFR (-1.3-fold), and upregulation of CASP3 (+1.7-fold) and BAX (+1.5-fold). Cytokines IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β decreased by 48.2%, 44.7%, and 39.5%, respectively, while IL-10 increased by 26.3%. Metabolomics showed a 2.8-fold increase in butyrate and ~35% reduction in oxidative stress. Microbiome diversity improved (Shannon index 2.8-3.6). Probiotic-derived metabolites modulate NF-κB, PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and apoptosis pathways, supporting their potential role as adjunct therapeutic agents in CRC management.

title: Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Reveal Mechanisms of Cardiovascular Protection Against Ponatinib-Induced Cardiotoxicity Through ROCKs Deletion in Cardiomyocytes.
abstract: Ponatinib is a potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor and primarily used in the treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph + ALL). Its broad anti-cancer capability is restricted to CML or Ph + ALL harboring T315I mutant breakpoint cluster region gene fused with the Abelson murine leukemia gene 1 due to its potential cardiotoxicity (CTX) side effect. It is crucial to better understand the mechanisms of ponatinib's CTX to maximize its beneficial therapeutic effects while reducing CTX. We established a ponatinib-induced CTX mouse model, which was used in this study for evaluating long-term effects of ponatinib on cardiac structure and function. We first assessed the role of Rho-associated coiled-coil containing kinases 1 and 2 (ROCK1 and ROCK2) in mediating CTX on mouse models characterized by the inducible cardiomyocyte-specific double ROCK knockout (DKO). Next, we expanded the study with single nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to reveal critical differentially expressed genes and interrelated biological pathways. Finally, we hypothesized the most probable underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms by synthesizing the mouse model and transcriptomic findings. Important findings include that double ROCK deletion in cardiomyocytes prevented ponatinib-induced cardiac dilation and dysfunction and suppressed serum levels of several vascular toxicity biomarkers. Analysis of snRNA-seq revealed cell-type-specific transcriptomic signatures attributable to ponatinib treatment; however, they were attenuated in DKO mouse hearts. The associated genes include extracellular matrix- and thrombogenesis-related genes in cardiomyocytes, myofibroblast activation-related genes in fibroblasts, and pathological activation-related genes in endothelial cells (EC). The hypothesized mechanism is to integrate transcriptomic signatures of these three functional associated cell types with prior established roles of ROCK1 and ROCK2 in regulating actin cytoskeleton rearrangement. Hence, the contributory roles of cardiomyocyte ROCK in CTX and vascular toxicity have opened a new field for future experimental validation: drug-activated ROCK activities and cytoskeleton reorganization occurred in cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts and EC form the driving forces responsible for CTX induction.

title: The first isolation, identification and pathogenicity of a goose-origin duck astrovirus type 3 strain.
abstract: To investigate the molecular epidemiological characteristics and pathogenicity of waterfowl astroviruses, tissue samples were collected from geese exhibiting suspected Duck astrovirus type 3 (DAstV-3) infection on a goose farm in Shandong Province of China. These samples underwent real-time RT-PCR detection, followed by virus isolation, whole-genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and pathogenicity challenge experiments. This study was the first to isolate a goose-origin DAstV-3 strain (DAstV-3/goose/shandong/2023/SD455), with a complete genome of 7,363 bp. Sequence analysis revealed that the strain was closest to domestically circulating DAstV-3 strains with 96.2-99.9% nucleotide identities. High variability in amino acid residues was predominantly observed in ORF1b (encoding RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) and ORF2 (encoding capsid protein) regions. Phylogenetic analysis clustered this strain within the DAstV-3 clade, forming a distinct sub-branch with the duck-origin reference strain Q3001 (bootstrap value = 92%). The pathogenicity tests conducted on 7-day-old goslings and ducklings demonstrated that the isolated strain caused similar clinical symptoms, followed by recovery. Histopathological examination revealed lesions in the lungs, liver, spleen, and kidneys, characterized by inflammation cell infiltration and parenchymal degeneration. The results of the epidemiological investigation showed that 88 DAstV-3 samples were detected from 13 provinces of the 15 provinces surveyed, and the positive rate of DAstV-3 was 6.51%. Among them, the positive rate of DAstV-3 in geese (5.15%) was slightly lower than that in ducks (7.14%). This study elucidated the cross-host transmission potential of goose-derived DAstV-3 among waterfowl and provided critical insights for viral surveillance and control strategies.

title: Ketohexokinase inhibitor discovery and clinical translation: Medicinal chemistry, tissue pharmacology, and biomarker-guided development.
abstract: Fructose metabolism exhibits pronounced flux- and tissue-specificity across the intestine, liver, kidneys and certain diseased tissues. Ketohexokinase (KHK) catalyses the phosphorylation of fructose to fructose 1-phosphate, thereby constituting a key metabolic node that links dietary or endogenous fructose exposure to adenosine triphosphate depletion, uric acid production, lipogenesis and cellular stress. KHK inhibition has recently emerged as an attractive strategy for treating metabolic diseases; however, its clinical translation faces a critical challenge in progressing from target modulation to genuine disease modification. Here, we review KHK isozyme biology and structural features, together with the mechanistic networks through which KHK mediates hepatic and extrahepatic metabolic injury. We then compare the structure-activity relationships, enzymatic and cellular potencies, pharmacokinetic properties, tissue exposure profiles and clinical development status of inhibitors representing distinct chemical scaffolds. PF-06835919 and LY3522348 have established that KHK can be pharmacologically modulated in humans, whereas ALN-KHK, a liver-targeted N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA therapeutic, has provided proof of concept for liver-selective gene silencing. Nevertheless, current clinical evidence remains largely confined to target engagement, short-term pharmacodynamic measures and reductions in hepatic steatosis, and is insufficient to demonstrate sustained improvements in histological or clinical outcomes. Future translation will require the stratification of patients with an active fructose-KHK axis, the integration of isozyme- and tissue-selective strategies, and validation against long-term endpoints capable of distinguishing target engagement from disease modification. Together, these measures could provide an actionable path towards the clinical implementation of KHK inhibitors.

title: Validity evidence for the Clinic Screening Tool for HIV (CST-HIV) addressing factors that undermine health-related quality of life in people living with HIV.
abstract: This study evaluated the psychometric properties and clinical validity of the Clinic Screening Tool for HIV (CST-HIV) to determine whether the CST-HIV demonstrates a reliable multidimensional structure and clinically meaningful associations with established patient-reported outcome measures (PROM) and HIV clinical markers. A cross-sectional study was conducted within the Spanish CoRIS multicentre cohort, including 286 adults with HIV. Participants completed the CST-HIV and validated PROMs. Clinical indicators (CD4+ cell count and percentage, HIV-1 RNA viral load, and non-AIDS events) were collected at current and retrospective time points. Analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, internal consistency, convergent and discriminant validity, associations with clinical markers, and age-group comparisons. Confirmatory factor analysis showed good model fit, with satisfactory internal consistency across domains (ω = 0.86-0.89). CST-HIV shows convergent validity, including psychological distress with PHQ-4 (r = 0.79), anticipated stigma with HIV stigma (r = 0.65), sexuality with sexual satisfaction (r = -0.74), sleep and fatigue with insomnia severity (r = 0.79), and material deprivation with social exclusion (r = 0.67) (all p < 0.001). Anticipated stigma (ρ = -0.16, p = 0.014) and material deprivation (ρ = -0.18, p = 0.005) were associated with lower CD4+ counts, while material deprivation was associated with higher viral load (ρ = 0.13, p = 0.046). Sexual satisfaction was lower among participants aged ≥50 years (d = -0.47, p < 0.001). The CST-HIV demonstrates strong psychometric performance, supporting its use as a valid, brief, multidimensional screening tool to inform person-centered HIV care and clinical intervention.

title: TNF-driven intracellular complement factor H-NF-κB feed-forward loop amplifies inflammatory mediator production in rheumatoid arthritis synovial fibroblasts.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves multiple pro-inflammatory cytokines; fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) are central effector cells that integrate these signals to produce pathogenic mediators. Tumor necrosis factor (TNF) is a major upstream driver of coordinated inflammatory mediator induction in FLS; however, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined, particularly intracellular feed-forward amplification sustaining and enhancing TNF-driven transcriptional outputs. Complement factor H (FH; gene CFH), a Sushi domain-only complement regulator, is elevated in RA serum. FH is regarded as an extracellular inhibitor of complement activation; however, its potential intracellular expression and functions in FLS have not been explored. We aimed to investigate intracellular FH expression and function using an in vitro transcribed messenger RNA (IVT mRNA)-based approach. FH expression in sera, synovial tissues, and fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) were assessed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR, and immunoblotting. To examine intracellular FH function, FLS were transfected with CFH-encoding IVT mRNA to express FH intracellularly, followed by next-generation sequencing (RNA-seq), RT-qPCR, ELISA, phosphorylation assays, and pathway inhibition. Interactions between TNF-driven signaling and intracellular FH were evaluated using TNF- and/or FH-neutralizing antibodies, with or without CFH-targeting small interfering RNA (siRNA). FH was highly expressed in RA synovium and predominantly localized intracellularly in FLS. To assess intracellular FH function, FLS were transfected with CFH-encoding IVT mRNA, which induced the coordinated upregulation of RA-relevant mediators, including granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), interleukin (IL)-8, IL-6, and multiple chemokines. Mechanistically, intracellular FH activated nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling, promoting receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 2 (RIPK2) phosphorylation and p65 nuclear translocation, and the competitive nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain 2 (NOD2) antagonist suppressed FH-driven gene induction. TNF and intracellular FH additively enhanced pathogenic mediator production. CFH-targeting siRNA attenuated TNF-induced cytokine and chemokine expression; blockade of extracellular FH had no detectable effect. Combined TNF neutralization and CFH knockdown produced more effective suppression of cytokine induction than either intervention alone. Intracellular FH is a previously unrecognized amplifier of TNF-driven inflammation in RA-FLS via a NOD2/RIPK2/NF-κB axis, establishing a feed-forward loop boosting pathogenic mediator production. Dual targeting of TNF and intracellular FH may represent a therapeutic strategy to suppress synovial inflammation more effectively.

title: YAP/AP-1 Activation in Sebocytes Promotes CCL5-Dependent Perifollicular Macrophage Recruitment in Rosacea.
abstract: Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder in which macrophages have been increasingly implicated, yet the spatial basis and local cues of their recruitment remain poorly defined. Given the prominent perifollicular inflammatory changes in rosacea, we investigated whether sebocytes contribute to macrophage recruitment and the underlying mechanisms. Multiplex immunofluorescence combined with distance-stratified quantification demonstrated a preferential perifollicular distribution of macrophages around pilosebaceous units (PSUs) in human rosacea lesions. Integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses identified the C-C motif chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5)-C-C motif chemokine receptor 5 (CCR5) axis as a candidate mediator of sebocyte-macrophage crosstalk. Silencing CCL5 by small interfering RNA and CCL5 neutralization attenuated sebocyte-driven macrophage migration in vitro and reduced macrophage accumulation in vivo. Transcriptomic analysis of sebocytes further linked CCL5 expression to activation of Yes-associated protein (YAP)/activator protein-1 (AP-1) signaling. Consistently, pharmacological inhibition of YAP or AP-1 reduced CCL5 expression in sebocytes and alleviated erythema and macrophage infiltration in vivo. Furthermore, untargeted lipidomics uncovered profound metabolic reprogramming in sebocytes, characterized notably by the accumulation of cholesteryl esters. Bidirectional interventions via simvastatin and cholesterol loading confirmed that this lipid remodeling acts as an upstream driver of YAP nuclear translocation. Overall, our study identifies a PSU-centered inflammatory niche in rosacea and implicates lipid-driven, YAP/AP-1-associated sebocytic CCL5 upregulation in perifollicular macrophage recruitment, providing a rationale for further exploring sebocyte- and pilosebaceous unit-directed therapeutic strategies in rosacea.

title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues
abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data for epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often ignore hierarchies among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-lineage hierarchies, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. Across simulated and real peripheral blood mononuclear cell, lung, and placental datasets, HOMED consistently yielded the highest PCCs and lowest RMSEs, outperforming existing scRNA-seq-guided DNAm deconvolution methods, improving accuracy, resolution, and cross-tissue generalizability.

title: The gut microbiota-derived butyrate improves gestational glucose homeostasis through HDAC3 inhibition and epigenetic activation of the SCGN/GLP-1 axis.
abstract: A deficiency in the gut microbiota-derived metabolite butyrate is associated with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet the causative molecular pathways remain undefined. Given its established role as a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor, we hypothesised that butyrate exerts its beneficial effects on gestational glucose homeostasis through epigenetic reprogramming of intestinal hormone secretion. We integrated clinical observation with causal experimentation. First, a nested case-control study measured serum butyrate and active GLP-1 in pregnant women. Second, a GDM mouse model induced by high-fat diet and antibiotics was treated with the butyrate-producing probiotic Clostridium butyricum for metabolic and microbial profiling. Colon tissues were analysed for HDAC expression and histone acetylation. Third, the mechanism was dissected in enteroendocrine cells using sodium butyrate, HDAC3 modulation, and integrated RNA-sequencing/H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing. Finally, HDAC3 heterozygous knockout mice were used for genetic validation. In the clinical cohort, serum butyrate and GLP-1 levels were consistently lower in women who developed GDM, evident both in early and mid-pregnancy (both p < 0.05). In mice, C. butyricum supplementation alleviated hyperglycaemia, insulin resistance, and circadian glucose rhythm disruption. This was paralleled by elevated systemic butyrate, enrichment of butyrate-producing gut bacteria, decreased colonic HDAC3 protein, and increased global histone H3K27 acetylation (H3K27ac). Multi-omics analysis in enteroendocrine cells identified secretagogin (SCGN) as a direct target gene, with butyrate enhancing both its transcription and promoter-associated H3K27ac. Consequently, butyrate and HDAC3 knockdown increased SCGN expression and GLP-1 secretion, whereas HDAC3 overexpression suppressed this axis-an effect reversible by co-treatment with butyrate. The metabolic improvements and SCGN upregulation driven by C. butyricum were abolished in HDAC3-haploinsufficient mice. We demonstrate that butyrate ameliorates GDM by specifically inhibiting intestinal HDAC3. This inhibition epigenetically activates the transcription of SCGN via enhanced H3K27ac, leading to potentiated GLP-1 secretion. Our work delineates a novel gut microbiota-epigenetic-hormonal axis, identifying HDAC3 and the downstream SCGN/GLP-1 pathway as potential targets for the prevention or treatment of GDM.

title: The impact of leukocyte-associated RNA retention on platelet RNA-based cancer detection.
abstract: Platelet RNA profiling is a promising liquid biopsy approach, offering minimally invasive insights into systemic diseases, such as cancer. Yet, the effect of leukocyte-associated RNA retention on platelet transcriptomic signatures remains unclear. This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of how leukocyte-associated RNA retention influences platelet RNA sequencing and machine learning (ML)-based cancer detection. Using the largest publicly available platelet transcriptomic dataset (2351 human RNA samples) and single-cell/single-platelet RNA sequencing from 29 donors, we quantified leukocyte-associated RNA retention in matched sample groups (low vs. high retention) via a novel 132-gene leukocyte marker panel. Diagnostic implications were assessed using 10 ML algorithms for binary classification (cancer vs. healthy), examining the contribution of leukocyte-derived transcripts. Interestingly, models trained on high-retention samples often showed slightly improved performance, suggesting complementary diagnostic value from leukocyte signals. Importantly, post hoc correction using remove unwanted variation (RUV) and linear modeling effectively mitigated retention effects. However, adding the leukocyte-associated RNA retention score to the full-cohort classifier changed cancer-detection AUC only minimally (0.9247 to 0.9249). Thus, whether this signal should be corrected, recalibrated, or reported should depend on the study question rather than assuming routine removal.
authors: Sjors G J G In 't Veld

title: Oral nicotine pouch extracts disrupt osteogenic differentiation in human embryonic stem cells.
abstract: Oral nicotine pouch (ONP) use has increased in recent years due to the perception that these products are a safer alternative to combustible tobacco products. However, little is known about the potential developmental toxicity of ONPs, particularly during bone formation. In this study, we evaluated the effects of ONP extracts from multiple ZYN flavors and nicotine concentrations on osteogenic differentiation using a human embryonic stem cell (hESC) model. H9 hESCs were differentiated toward the osteogenic lineage and continuously exposed to ONP extracts throughout differentiation. Cellular metabolic activity was assessed using the MTT assay, while ATP content, total protein content, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activity, and calcium deposition were evaluated using biochemical assays and Alizarin Red S staining. Gene expression was assessed using RT-qPCR and single-cell RNA sequencing, followed by pseudotime trajectory and transcriptomic point of departure (tPOD) analyses. ONP exposure caused concentration-dependent reductions in MTT activity, ATP content, total protein content, ALP activity, GPx activity, and calcium deposition. Expression of the osteogenic marker RUNX2 was generally decreased following ONP exposure, while TWIST1, SOX10, and TBX5 expression were increased in several treatment groups. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrated significant alterations in cell cluster distribution and pseudotime trajectory following ONP exposure, suggesting disrupted osteogenic lineage progression. Transcriptomic analysis further identified widespread perturbation of bone development-related genes across treatments. Wintergreen 6 mg had among the greatest transcriptomic potency metrics. Together, these findings reveal that ONP extracts disrupt osteogenic differentiation in hESCs and alter developmental lineage progression. This study provides mechanistic evidence that oral nicotine pouch extracts perturb early osteogenic differentiation in a human stem cell model and supports further evaluation of their developmental toxicity.

title: Differential expression of lung-homing chemokine receptors in severe COVID-19: distinct profiles between Alpha and Omicron.
abstract: Severe Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), is characterized by excessive pulmonary immune cell recruitment mediated by chemokine - chemokine receptor signaling. Variant-specific differences in lung-homing chemokine receptor expression remain insufficiently defined. This retrospective case-control study analyzed Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid (BALF) samples from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admitted patients with severe COVID-19 during the Alpha (hICU-α) and Omicron (hICU-Ο) waves, along with SARS-CoV-2 - negative controls. Messenger RNA expression of CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCR3, CCR2, and CCR6 was quantified by Real-Time quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-qPCR). Protein expression of selected receptors was assessed by western blotting in available samples. CXCR1 expression was significantly increased in hICU-α patients compared with controls (p = 0.02) but not in hICU-Ο patients. CXCR2 expression was elevated in both hICU-α and hICU-Ο groups versus controls (p = 0.008 and p = 0.006, respectively) and was higher in hICU-α than hICU-Ο patients (p = 0.009). CXCR3 expression was increased in both COVID-19 groups compared with controls (p = 0.03 and p = 0.001). CCR6 expression was highest in hICU-Ο patients compared with hICU-α and controls (p = 0.04 and p = 0.001). Increased CXCR2 and CXCR3 protein expression was confirmed in hICU-Ο patients. Severe COVID-19 is associated with variant-specific alterations in lung chemokine receptor expression, highlighting differential immune trafficking patterns during Alpha and Omicron waves.

title: Single-Cell Omics Profiling Reveals Enhanced Heterogeneity of Cord Blood Basophils at Birth.
abstract: Basophils are important mediators in the pathobiology of atopic diseases, yet the heterogeneity of basophils within the perinatal environment remains incompletely understood. In our study, we aimed to perform comprehensive profiling of paired maternal and cord blood basophils using a single-cell omics approach to look into their distinct transcriptional signatures. Basophils were isolated from four paired maternal-cord blood samples at the time of delivery, including one mother who delivered monozygotic twins. Basophil characterization of maternal blood (MB) and cord blood (CB) was analyzed in flow cytometry. Single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed to further examine the basophils composition and heterogeneity in MB and CB. We observed that CB basophils have lower expression of FCER1A, and no cell-bound or circulating IgE levels as compared to MB. Our scRNA-seq data show that MB and CB basophils are different in both transcriptomic and functional profiles. CB basophils exhibit greater heterogeneity than MB. Low interindividual variability between twin CB basophil samples confirmed that the transcriptomic difference between MB and CB basophils is biologically meaningful. Trajectory pseudotime analysis revealed that CB basophils have an earlier pseudotime, potentially indicating a more naïve state. In addition, we demonstrated that CB basophils exhibit distinct functional capacities. Our data identified protein and gene signatures in MB and CB basophils. We demonstrated that CB has greater heterogeneity than MB basophils, thereby highlighting the relevance of single cell profiling of basophils in the context of the maternal-fetal interface.

title: TAF9B promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression through TBP-dependent transcriptional activation of ADAM17.
abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is one of the common malignant tumors. TATA protein-associated factor 9B (TAF9B) is essential for regulating RNA polymerase II-mediated transcription, and this regulation at the transcriptional level, which is closely related to the carcinogenesis of various tumors, represents a complex process. This study aimed to investigate the expression of TAF9B in ESCC and its potential effect on patient prognosis. Real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction analysis showed that the expression level of TAF9B was significantly upregulated in ESCC tissues (P = 0.0039). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated that patients with low TAF9B expression exhibited better overall survival than those with high TAF9B expression (P = 0.01). This study indicated that TAF9B is highly expressed in ESCC and may have prognostic relevance for ESCC patients. Further studies revealed that TAF9B knockdown could inhibit the proliferation of ESCC cells both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptome sequencing analysis and validation experiments confirmed that a disintegrin and metalloproteinase 17 (ADAM17) acts as a downstream target gene regulated by TAF9B. Our study demonstrated that TAF9B promotes TATA binding protein occupancy at the ADAM17 promoter and upregulates ADAM17 expression. This process further activates the TNF-α/NF-κB signaling pathway and suppresses apoptosis in ESCC cells. Collectively, TAF9B acts as a novel oncogenic factor in ESCC and promotes tumor progression.

title: Mechanism study on CSF3-Induced M2 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages and CCL9 secretion in promoting tumor progression in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) accounts for ∼85% of head and neck cancers and is the sixth most common malignancy worldwide. Standard surgery plus chemoradiotherapy has limited success due to high recurrence. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in the tumor microenvironment (TME) promote tumor growth, invasion and angiogenesis. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor 3 (CSF3) regulates neutrophil function and may influence monocyte differentiation into M2 macrophages in breast and bladder cancers. This study aims to investigate CSF3's role in promoting TAM-M2 polarization in HNSCC and explore the mechanisms using in vitro and in vivo approaches. Bioinformatic methods analyzed CSF3's clinicopathological significance and association with M2 infiltration. CSF3 expression was evaluated in paired tumor/normal tissues by RT-qPCR and IHC, and serum levels by ELISA. CSF3-modulated cell lines were co-cultured with TAMs; polarization was assessed via marker expression by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry. CSF3-overexpressing mouse models examined tumor growth and CD206 expression by IHC. Functional assays on MOC2 cells used TAM-conditioned supernatant. RNA-seq and CCL9 secretion were analyzed. CSF3 correlated with poor prognosis and increased M2 infiltration. Elevated CSF3 mRNA/protein were detected in tumor tissues and serum. CSF3 overexpression promoted M2 polarization, CD206 expression, and tumor growth. Conditioned medium from TAMs co-cultured with CSF3-knockdown tumor cells attenuated MOC2 proliferation, migration and invasion. Tumor-derived CSF3 upregulated TAM-derived CCL9, and exogenous CCL9 restored pro-tumor effects. Elevated CSF3 in HNSCC promotes TAM-M2 polarization and induces CCL9 production in polarized TAMs, creating a pro-tumor microenvironment that facilitates HNSCC progression.

title: Transcriptome analysis of mRNA and long non-coding RNA profiles in the brains of CVA10-infected suckling mice.
abstract: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) caused by Coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) remains an important public health concern. Although most infections are self-limiting, severe cases may develop neurological complications, including acute flaccid paralysis and aseptic meningitis. However, host transcriptional responses to CVA10 infection within the central nervous system (CNS) remain poorly understood. Here, we established a CVA10-infected ICR suckling mouse model and performed transcriptomic profiling of brain tissues using RNA-seq, followed by RT-qPCR validation. A total of 243 differentially expressed mRNAs and 776 differentially expressed lncRNAs were identified in the brains of CVA10-infected mice. Interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as Ifit1 exhibited significant dysregulation in CVA10-infected brain tissue. Integrated GO and KEGG functional enrichment analyses revealed that these genes were significantly associated with innate immune and inflammatory responses, particularly interferon-related signaling pathways. Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified ten immune-related hub genes, including Irf7, Rsad2, Isg15, Stat1, Ifih1, Ifit1, Ifit3, Oasl2, Rtp4 and Usp18. RT-qPCR validation showed overall agreement with RNA-seq findings, supporting the reliability of the transcriptomic analysis. Long non coding RNAs can extensively regulate these immune-related genes in both directions. These results offer a foundation for further investigation of the molecular basis of CVA10-related neurological disease, and for exploring candidate biomarkers and molecular targets.

title: An m5C-associated NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF programme marks melanoma cell states and immune features.
abstract: RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C)-associated programmes may help characterise melanoma cell states and their immune context. We investigated an NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF (NYC) programme using patient-matched sequencing, experimental perturbation and multiscale transcriptomic analyses. We analysed m5C-MeRIP-seq and matched Input RNA data from three melanoma-adjacent-normal patient pairs, using a paired edgeR interaction model for regional IP enrichment. Tissue and cell experiments included NSUN5 knockdown, CENPF-targeted MeRIP-qPCR and western blotting. Clinical analyses considered proliferation and sampling site. Trajectory and regulatory inference were restricted to malignant cells from GSE215120, with patient-level summaries. Treatment-associated changes were examined in 43 paired patients from GSE91061. Computational perturbation and transcriptomic signature reversal prioritised candidate regulators and compounds. Two CENPF regions showed increased relative IP enrichment after Input adjustment (4.97- and 5.85-fold; BH q = 0.0457 and 0.0074). NSUN5 knockdown reduced CENPF m5C enrichment and protein abundance. NYC was associated with proliferation; its survival association did not persist after proliferation adjustment. Within malignant cells, NYC-High retained an association with an immune-resistance expression programme after G2M/E2F and depth adjustment (nine patients; BH q = 0.0156). Regulatory analyses prioritised MLX, whose simulated knockout and overexpression produced opposing reference-flow alignments (BH q = 0.0134 and 0.0201). MLX regulon activity was associated with glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation after adjustment. In GSE91061, responders showed a greater treatment-associated NYC decrease than non-responders (mean change difference -0.209; permutation P = 0.0138). Drug screening generated candidates for experimental testing. NYC provides an m5C-associated framework connecting patient-derived molecular observations to malignant-cell states and immune features. YBX1 remains a candidate reader, and regulatory, treatment-associated and drug-prioritisation findings do not establish a complete causal pathway or a clinically validated predictive biomarker.

title: Estrogen-driven PDK4-MYH9 phosphorylation promotes mitochondrial fission and osteogenic commitment of mesenchymal stem cells.
abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP), driven primarily by estrogen deficiency, represents a major public health challenge. Although estrogen's anti-resorptive effects are well established, the direct osteogenic actions by which it regulates the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate a novel mechanism by which estrogen regulates osteogenic differentiation in MSCs and to identify key downstream molecular events. We employed single-cell RNA sequencing to profile the transcriptional landscape of osteoporotic MSCs. The pro-osteogenic effects of estradiol (E2) were validated in ovariectomized mice and primary mouse bone marrow-derived MSCs through in vitro differentiation assays and mitochondrial functional analyses. Downstream targets of estrogen receptor were identified by integrating CUT&Tag-seq with transcriptomic data and validated using conditional knockout mice. Protein interactions and phosphorylation sites were mapped via co-immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, site-directed mutagenesis, and mitochondrial morphology assays. Osteoporotic MSCs displayed concurrent impairments in osteogenic differentiation and mitochondrial function. E2 stimulated mitochondrial fission, enhanced maximal respiration, and induced DRP1 translocation to mitochondria. The combined evidence from our CUT&Tag-seq, RNA-seq, and the additional CUT&Tag-qPCR and ERα knockdown data supports the conclusion that Pdk4 is a direct transcriptional target of ERα. This finding is further corroborated by the compromised osteogenesis observed in conditional Pdk4 knockout mice. Mechanistically, PDK4 catalyzed MYH9 phosphorylation at serine 1943, thereby facilitating DRP1 recruitment to mitochondria and subsequent fission. Both pharmacological inhibition of PDK4 and introduction of the phosphorylation-deficient MYH9 S1943A mutant abolished the E2-induced effects. Notably, Pdk4 overexpression in ovariectomized mice reversed bone loss in the absence of exogenous estrogen. This study identifies an unrecognized ERα-PDK4-MYH9 signaling axis through which estrogen drives mitochondrial fission to promote osteogenic differentiation of MSCs. These findings expand the current understanding of estrogen's skeletal actions by revealing a pro-osteogenic effect on MSCs, and suggest PDK4 as a potential candidate for therapeutic exploration in PMOP.

title: Extracellular matrix remodeling and regulated cell-death-immune associations in adhesive capsulitis: a three-cohort transcriptomic analysis.
abstract: Adhesive capsulitis (AC) is a fibroinflammatory disorder characterized by painful shoulder restriction and progressive capsular fibrosis. Whether regulated cell-death (RCD) programs are consistently altered across independent transcriptomic cohorts remains uncertain. We reanalyzed three public bulk RNA-seq cohorts. GSE140731 was the discovery cohort (22 AC and 26 shoulder-instability surgical controls), and GSE190023 and GSE238053 were independent validation cohorts. Differential expression was estimated from filtered raw counts with PyDESeq2, with age/sex adjustment in GSE140731. Curated pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and necroptosis gene sets; immune marker-gene scores; pathway enrichment; STRING network structure; cross-cohort concordance; an exploratory three-gene classifier; and qPCR validation of four selected genes in TGF-β1-stimulated SW982 cells were evaluated. The adjusted discovery analysis identified 439 upregulated and 113 downregulated genes at FDR < 0.05. ECM-receptor interaction was strongly positively enriched (NES = 2.299, q = 0.001), making extracellular-matrix remodeling the clearest pathway-level signal. RCD findings were mixed: pyroptosis was not different (delta = -0.105, q = 0.708), ferroptosis was lower but borderline after FDR correction (delta = -0.426, q = 0.056), and necroptosis was lower (delta = -0.320, q = 0.035); the core necroptosis gene set was also negatively enriched (NES = -1.673, q = 0.038). Six immune marker scores were FDR-significant in discovery, but none replicated at cohort-wise FDR significance in the validation cohorts. Cross-cohort gene-effect concordance was heterogeneous (Spearman rho = -0.047 for GSE190023 and 0.383 for GSE238053). The COL11A1-SPON2-PITPNC1 classifier achieved a pooled out-of-fold AUC of 0.820 (95% CI, 0.684-0.930) in GSE140731; external-cohort AUCs ranged from 0.750 to 0.812 with wide confidence intervals, and non-nested feature selection precluded claims of clinical utility. qPCR showed higher COL11A1 and SPON2 and lower PLA2G4A expression after TGF-β1 stimulation, whereas PITPNC1 did not differ significantly, providing model-specific support without establishing causal or clinical validity. Across the three cohorts, ECM remodeling was the most reproducible feature of AC, whereas RCD- and immune-related signals were cohort-dependent and did not support uniform activation of pyroptosis, ferroptosis, or necroptosis. The classifier and RCD signatures remain hypothesis-generating. The SW982 qPCR results provide model-specific experimental support for selected candidates, but broader functional validation in primary AC tissues and cells is required.

title: Integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-Seq analysis reveals a LCR-related prognostic signature for precision prognostication and therapeutic stratification in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: Lysine crotonylation (LCR) is an emerging post-translational modification, yet its clinical significance and therapeutic relevance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remain poorly understood. Multi-omics data were collected from public repositories. Consensus clustering based on 18 LCR-related genes (LCRGs) was performed to define molecular subtypes. Co-expression modules identified via WGCNA were integrated into 101 machine-learning combinations to establish a LCR-related signature (LCRS). The signature was evaluated for survival prediction, immune microenvironment characteristics, and drug response across multiple cohorts, complemented by single-cell RNA sequencing. Candidate therapeutic targets and compounds were screened using DepMap CRISPR dependency data and pharmacogenomic databases (CTRP and PRISM). Two distinct molecular subtypes (C1 and C2) were identified, displaying significant differences in survival, immune infiltration, and signaling pathways. Integrating WGCNA hub genes with an optimal machine-learning framework yielded a robust 15-gene LCRS, which served as an independent prognostic factor in the TCGA cohorts. Single-cell analysis localized signature genes predominantly to endothelial cells. Pharmacogenomic profiling indicated higher sensitivity to sunitinib among high-risk patients, whereas low-risk patients displayed elevated sensitivity to axitinib and pazopanib. Furthermore, dependency screening prioritized CLCNKA as a key therapeutic target along with ten candidate compounds for high-risk patients. This study establishes a robust LCR-related prognostic signature and nominates CLCNKA as a novel therapeutic vulnerability, offering actionable insights for personalized stratification and treatment in ccRCC.

title: LILRB3 as an ulcerative colitis-associated molecular biomarker: integrated transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental validation.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by mucosal inflammation and immune dysregulation. Although macrophage-mediated inflammation is associated with UC progression, its molecular basis remains incompletely understood. This study integrated bioinformatic analyses and experimental validation to identify UC-associated molecular biomarkers and explore their roles in immune dysregulation. Bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated for differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and multi-algorithm machine learning. The machine-learning model was evaluated in independent validation cohorts, and a nomogram was subsequently constructed and evaluated in an additional colonic-tissue cohort. Immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication, pseudotime analysis, and scTenifoldKnk-based virtual knockout were used to investigate hub genes. RT-qPCR, WB, and IHC validated the findings in a DSS-induced mouse model and clinical samples, while siRNA-mediated LILRB3 knockdown was performed in THP-1-derived macrophages. Differential expression analysis and WGCNA identified 55 candidate genes. Through screening of 127 machine-learning algorithm combinations, DPP10, LILRB3, MTMR11, and SLC6A14 were identified as UC-associated molecular biomarkers. A separately constructed logistic regression nomogram showed an apparent AUC of 0.989. LILRB3 was predominantly expressed in myeloid cells, particularly M1 macrophages, and was associated with inflammatory immune cell infiltration. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed that LILRB3⁺ M1 macrophages exhibited active intercellular communication involving MHC-II-CD4 and other inflammation-related signaling pathways. Experimental validation showed increased PirB expression in the colonic tissues of DSS-induced colitis mice and elevated LILRB3 expression in human UC colonic tissues. Knockdown of LILRB3 in THP-1-derived macrophages significantly reduced TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β mRNA expression. LILRB3 is a candidate UC-associated molecular biomarker in colonic tissue and may be associated with proinflammatory macrophage remodeling and myeloid immune dysregulation, warranting mechanistic investigation.

title: WGCNA and single-cell analysis identify FLG, DSG3 and DSG1 as melanoma-associated hub genes and their modulation by Dinaciclib.
abstract: Melanoma is one of the most aggressive skin cancers, and its molecular heterogeneity continues to present challenges for diagnosis and treatment. Identification of molecular alterations associated with melanoma progression may provide clinically relevant biomarkers and therapeutic insights. In this study, differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were integrated across melanoma transcriptomic datasets to identify disease-associated gene modules and hub genes. Protein-protein interaction analysis and prognostic modelling were subsequently used to characterize candidate desmosomal genes. WGCNA identified melanoma-associated modules enriched in keratinization, epidermal differentiation, and desmosome-related processes, with FLG, DSG1, and DSG3 emerging as prominent hub genes. Their prognostic relevance was evaluated in the TCGA-SKCM cohort using LASSO-Cox and multivariable survival analysis, while single-cell RNA sequencing was used to investigate their cellular distribution. The analysis revealed distinct cellular expression patterns, with DSG3 showing expression within melanoma cells, whereas FLG and DSG1 were predominantly associated with keratinocyte populations. Pharmacological validation using Dinaciclib in A375 and SK-MEL-28 melanoma cells demonstrated reduced cell viability and increased accumulation of cells in the G2/M phase, accompanied by reduced expression of FLG, DSG1, and DSG3. Molecular docking further predicted potential interactions of Dinaciclib with FLG and DSG3. Collectively, these findings identify a melanoma-associated desmosomal gene program with prognostic relevance and demonstrate that Dinaciclib treatment modulates the expression of these genes in melanoma cells.
